methodological_rigor.justification: The study uses a layered experimental approach combining unbiased compound screening (144 compounds), multiple BRCA-proficient and BRCA-mutant ovarian cancer cell lines, xenografts, PDX models, and patient-derived organoids. Mechanistic dissection includes RNA-seq, metabolomics, 15N-glutamine metabolic flux tracing, Co-IP, PLA, and AlphaFold3 structural predictions validated experimentally. Statistical analyses are appropriate (two-sided Student's t-test, two-way ANOVA, Kaplan-Meier, Bliss synergy, Pearson correlation) with 3+ biological replicates; authors acknowledge lack of multiple testing correction in some analyses.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is entirely preclinical (cell lines, xenografts, PDX, organoids) - maps to Oxford LoE 5 by definition. Translational relevance is strong because it identifies a mechanistically defined combination strategy (elesclomol-copper + PARPi, with de novo pyrimidine synthesis targeting for resistance) in an FDA-approved PARPi-resistant ovarian cancer context, directly informing near-term clinical trial design.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods are comprehensive with detailed cell line authentication, ethics approval numbers (NCC2022A371; 22/328-3530), randomization described for xenograft experiments, tumor volume formula specified, and humane endpoints defined. RNA-seq data deposited in GEO (GSE246085). Compound screening normalized data provided in Supplementary Data 1. Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary referenced. Some ARRIVE items (blinding of outcome assessors, sample size justification) not explicitly addressed.

novelty_literature.justification: The study presents several novel mechanistic insights: copper directly binds ATRIP (not ATR) at C-terminal cysteine residues (C624, C630, C680, C682) to disrupt ATR-ATRIP interaction, a mechanism distinct from cuproptosis and FDX1-independent. Identification of de novo pyrimidine synthesis as a secondary adaptive vulnerability in resistant tumors adds further originality. The work extends prior cuproptosis/ATR literature in a novel mechanistic direction with therapeutic implications.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well-organized with logical progression from screen to mechanism to resistance biology to therapeutic rescue. Figure legends are detailed with sample sizes, statistical tests, and p-value reporting. BioRender schematics aid comprehension. Some sections are dense but overall clarity is strong, and main findings are communicated effectively.

key_strengths: Rigorous unbiased compound screening identifying elesclomol as a top synergizer with PARPi in BRCA-proficient ovarian cancer
Mechanistic validation of copper-ATRIP direct binding using AlphaFold3 predictions confirmed by metal-loaded resin pulldowns, Co-IP, and PLA
Integration of multiple preclinical models: cell lines, xenografts, PDX, and patient-derived organoids
Identification of de novo pyrimidine synthesis as an actionable secondary vulnerability in PARPi-resistant tumors with metabolic flux tracing evidence
Data deposition (GEO GSE246085) and appropriate ethics/animal protocol documentation
key_concerns: All findings are preclinical; no human efficacy or toxicity data beyond PDX/organoid models
Drug-adapted resistance was induced by short-term (7-14 day) exposure, potentially not fully recapitulating clinical resistance
Combination dosing thresholds in mice (50 mg/kg olaparib, 5-10 mg/kg elesclomol) may not directly translate to human pharmacology
Sample sizes for IHC quantification (n=5) and some in vitro replicates are modest
chief_reviewer.rationale: Strong mechanistic preclinical study with translational appeal for PARPi resistance, multi-model validation, and novel copper-ATRIP biochemistry, fitting Tier 2 (Nature Communications/Cancer Research caliber) with minor revisions.
